hr.title: Running leave as HR
hr.intro: Set up once, then Leave Ledger tells you what is due and drafts what you send.

steps.t: Tell Leave Ledger about your company
steps.d: Settings. Your headcount and holidays decide which California leave laws apply to you.

steps.t: Bring in your employees
steps.d: Employees, then Import from a file. Upload the employee list your HR or payroll system exports, Excel or CSV. Leave Ledger matches the columns, and you see every row before anything is saved.

steps.t: Invite your team to sign in
steps.d: Users. Each employee signs in with Google and sees only their own leave. Managers see dates, never reasons.

steps.t: Start each day on Today
steps.d: Every deadline you owe by law, soonest first. Tick a step when it is done.

steps.t: Open a leave that needs approval
steps.d: Leaves. The plan shows the protected dates, what the state pays, and whether the employee qualifies.

steps.t: Check what the manager will read
steps.d: The manager gets the dates and what not to do. Never the reason, the type of leave, or anything medical.

steps.t: Approved
steps.d: The employee now sees a green Confirmed on their leave page, and the manager has the dates.

steps.t: Send the letters the law requires
steps.d: Leave Ledger drafts each letter from the plan. Read it, edit it, then mark it sent. The employee can read it on their leave page.

mgr.title: Leave for managers
mgr.intro: You see when your team is out and plan coverage. The reasons stay with HR.

steps.t: See who is out
steps.d: My team shows the next 12 weeks. You see dates only, never why.

steps.t: HR tells you when a leave is approved
steps.d: You get the dates, the expected return, and what to do and not do. It also comes by email when your company has it set up.

steps.t: Plan coverage
steps.d: Write who covers what. HR sees your plan on the leave.

steps.t: Heard someone needs time off? Tell HR the same day
steps.d: The legal clock starts when you hear about it, even if they never say the word leave. Keep it short, no medical details.

emp.title: Asking for time off
emp.intro: Find out what you qualify for, send the request, and follow it until it is confirmed.

steps.t: See what you have
steps.d: My leave shows your sick hours, family leave, and about how much the state pays while you are out.

steps.t: Learn your options
steps.d: Guide explains each California leave in plain words: how long, what it pays, who qualifies.

steps.t: Not sure which leave fits? Start here
steps.d: Pick what is going on. A few questions, and nothing is sent until you say so.

steps.t: See your protection and pay first
steps.d: The dates your job is protected and what the state may pay, worked out for you.

steps.t: Check it and send it to HR
steps.d: The request is filled in from your answers. Change anything, then send it.

steps.t: Follow your request
steps.d: Sent to HR, then HR reviewing, then Confirmed. HR replies within 5 business days.

steps.t: Look for the green Confirmed
steps.d: When HR approves, your dates are confirmed. Your manager is told the dates only, never the reason.

steps.t: Get paid by the state, step by step
steps.d: File with EDD using the dates and links here. Tick each step as you go.
